properties.name: 1623 Farnam
properties.notes: Omaha's carrier hotel: a nine-story, ~75,000 sq ft facility with around 8 MW of capacity at 1623 Farnam Street downtown, home to the OmahaIX internet exchange and some 60 carriers. News Press & Gazette Co. subsidiary Berks Group acquired Nebraska Data Centers and the 1623 Farnam carrier hotel in 2018 and established 1623 Farnam LLC — so 'Nebraska Data Centers' as an operator name is HISTORICAL, not current. Build-out history: a $10 million expansion in 2019 built out the fifth floor, floors six through nine were added in 2021, and the final two data halls completed in June 2025 added 1.5 MW of IT capacity and space for 280 racks. CEO Bill Severn cites 'significant demand from AI workloads, edge deployments, content platforms, and broadband networks'. The company is separately planning an OMA2 campus expansion explicitly aimed at AI and edge infrastructure growth, with no site, size or date disclosed on its own page — a LEAD to re-check, not yet a proposable facility. DCD also reports the facility serves Trump Media & Technology Group; that is a tenant claim DCD attributes to other reporting and is deliberately NOT recorded as a structured field. capacityMw is the ~8 MW total, not the 1.5 MW increment; investmentUsd records ONLY the sourced $10M 2019 fifth-floor expansion, since no total site capex is published. Coordinates are a street-address approximation.

properties.name: 5C Group / Vultr Data Center (Prime Ohio)
properties.operator: 5C Group (Hypertec Cloud + 5C Data Centers); tenant Vultr (The Constant Company, LLC)
properties.notes: 5C Group (formed May 2025 when Hypertec Cloud acquired 5C Data Centers) owns/builds the campus in the Prime Ohio corporate park; Vultr (legal entity The Constant Company, LLC) is the AI/cloud tenant. Corrects a discovery-pipeline conflation of this project with a separate, independently tax-credited Crusoe Energy Systems project elsewhere in Springfield -- not the same facility. Capacity: 75 MW disclosed operating load at opening vs. 150 MW max design load (city FAQ) -- both real, tracked field carries the larger design figure. Investment: ~$1.3B total project cost (multi-source) vs. $901.3M JobsOhio incentive-scoped committed investment -- tracked field carries the total-project figure. 120 permanent jobs / >$14M annual payroll disclosed (WYSO); a separate JobsOhio incentive filing cites 20 committed data-infrastructure jobs (narrower, incentive-scoped count). Incentives: ~$95M city enterprise-zone abatement over 15 years; $32M+ state 10-year 50% Ohio Tax Credit Authority credit (Oct 2025) to The Constant Company. Community context: Springfield passed a 6-month moratorium on new data centers and a citizen petition to ban them was launched; Clark County (Jul 2026) restricted data centers to I-2 heavy-industrial zoning, but the county's own zoning administrator noted no I-2 parcels currently exist in county jurisdiction, and Springfield Township (where Prime Ohio sits) zones separately from the county -- this rule change may not directly bind this site.

properties.name: 60 Hudson Street
properties.operator: Multi-tenant carrier hotel (Hudson Interxchange, Digital Realty, DataBank, Equinix, and 100+ telecom tenants)
properties.notes: Landmarked 1930 Art Deco former Western Union building in TriBeCa, Manhattan — the East Coast's most important carrier hotel / interconnection point, hosting 100+ telecom and data-center tenants. Represented as ONE consolidated facility record rather than one per tenant, since the physical building is the meaningful unit. Total building size is 1,149,619 sq ft, 24 stories + basement, per an authoritative SEC EDGAR CMBS filing (2023) — this is whole-building square footage, not data-center-specific space. No whole-building data-center power (MW) figure is disclosed by any verifiable primary source; a 50MW figure appears on aggregator sites but traces to an unverified 2014 reference and is not repeated here as fact. The one solidly-verified tenant figure: Hudson Interxchange (HIX) occupies ~173,000 sq ft with a 15MW Con Edison feed (+2MW expansion announced), confirmed via Data Center Dynamics (2024-08-21). Figures for Digital Realty and DataBank's space in this building could not be independently confirmed from primary sources in this research pass (conflicting numbers across aggregator sites) and are deliberately omitted rather than guessed — capacityMw is left unset for the same reason (no reliable whole-building total exists). Coordinates are a building-level geocode from a map aggregator, not independently verified against a primary GIS source.

properties.name: Aligned Data Centers – Conesville Industrial Park
properties.notes: Brownfield redevelopment of former AEP Conesville coal plant (2 GW, operational 62 years, closed May 2020). Frontier Group of Companies acquired the plant in 2020 and built the Conesville Industrial Park across ~2,500 acres; Aligned purchased a 197-acre parcel. Aligned describes the project as 'AI/HPC' and 'Gigascale' in its press materials, and this is its third Ohio campus (others: Perkins Township/Sandusky, 96 MW total; Pataskala). Multi-building campus — renderings show up to four buildings; second, third, and fourth buildings referenced at groundbreaking. Capacity MW not publicly disclosed. Investment described as 'multi-billion dollar' — no firm figure confirmed; field omitted per policy. Construction jobs described as 'thousands'; permanent roles as 'hundreds of high-quality long-term positions' — projections only, numeric fields omitted. Aligned is exploring on-site nuclear power (SMRs) for this campus and nearby Zanesville/Cambridge sites; no agreement confirmed. Coordinates approximate (village-level). Site infrastructure funding note: the Coshocton Port Authority received a $58.7M grant (Ohio Dept of Development All Ohio Future Fund, announced July 21, 2025) for utility upgrades, water/wastewater extensions, and roadway improvements across the broader industrial park — this benefits Aligned indirectly but is not a direct subsidy to Aligned and is therefore not listed under subsidies.

properties.name: Aligned Data Centers — Pataskala
properties.notes: Blocked 200 MW campus (89 acres, 3 planned buildings, down from 4) at Broad St & Mink St in the Pataskala industrial park, which would have run on on-site Bloom Energy natural-gas fuel cells. The Planning & Zoning Commission voted 5–2 on 2026-06-03 to recommend rejection (staff had recommended approval), and City Council rejected the site plan 7-0 on 2026-08-25. Recorded as cancelled because the city denied the application; note that Aligned itself has not abandoned the project — its general counsel said the company would “reflect and regroup.” A citizen charter amendment banning data centers over 25 MW goes to Pataskala and Granville voters on Nov. 3, 2026. Coordinates approximate (Pataskala city-center).

properties.name: Alterra Marshall Technology & Energy Center
properties.notes: Proposed data center (Marshall Technology & Energy Center, MTEC) plus a co-located natural-gas electric generation facility within Brooks Industrial Park, Marshall. WWMT (2026-04) resolves the load split that earlier reporting left open: up to 1,400 MW required at full buildout, around 1,000 MW of that from on-site gas turbines and up to 400 MW imported from the grid at peak — so capacityMw.planned is the campus power requirement and the 1 GW plant is carried both in energy.onSiteGenerationMw and as its own power_generation record. ~270 acres (112 buildable), roughly half wetlands. Alterra (Toronto-based) estimates 300-500 direct high-skill jobs. Mayor Wolfersberger (2026-01) called it "just a concept" with "no site plans or utility agreements yet"; due diligence runs into Q3 2026, then construction is "probably 18 months to two years away" if approved. Land is already zoned heavy industrial, so no public referendum is required (unlike Augusta Township). Planned closed-loop liquid cooling. Coordinates are an approximate Marshall-area estimate, not parcel-geocoded; the LDFA purchase price ($1.12M) is for land only, not a project investment figure.

properties.name: AVAIO Digital Perseus
properties.notes: Redevelopment of the former Delta View Golf Course (76 acres) into a 3-phase Pittsburg Technology Park; Phase 1 is the ~300,000 sq ft Perseus Data Center, targeting first occupancy in 2027. Status corrected to 'permitted' (not 'proposed'): the project holds a CEC opt-in certification (99 MW, Dec 8 2025) and a City of Pittsburg Commercial Design Review approval (Dec 11 2025, modified Feb 12 2026); no source confirms groundbreaking/construction has started. capacityMw.planned=99 reflects the CEC-certified figure, superseding an earlier ~92MW target; the Specific Plan's long-term ceiling of up to 500MW across the full technology park is undated/speculative and not recorded here. Investment ($800M+) is AVAIO's own Dec 2024 disclosure, widely syndicated but not independently audited. Jobs figures are not disclosed anywhere found and are omitted. aiClassification set to 'likely': AVAIO's own materials use explicit 'AI and cloud-driven deployments' language but do not publish GPU/HPC-specific technical specs. The Center for Biological Diversity's CEQA lawsuit (Case No. N24-2162, filed Dec 2024) was SETTLED in Dec 2025 (CBD agreed not to oppose Phase 1 in exchange for 100% renewable/carbon-free electricity, rooftop solar, 100% recycled water for cooling, wildlife monitoring, and a $750,000 community climate-resiliency payment) - it is not an active legal threat, though broader public opposition continues (see community).

properties.name: AVAIO Digital Taurus
properties.notes: Distinct from AVAIO's 'Leo' campus in Little Rock/Pulaski County AR — do not conflate. Site: East Metropolitan Center Business and Industrial Park, Brandon. Land acreage: AVAIO's own project page and groundbreaking materials cite 329 acres; the August 19 press release cited 175 acres — 329 used as more authoritative per operator's site. Capacity: 116 MW initial via executed ESA with Entergy Mississippi (energized June 2027 per operator site); Entergy guiding an additional 420 MW of grid power available by end of 2030; access to Gulf South Pipeline for up to 500 MW of on-site behind-the-meter thermal generation starting Q2 2027 — total baseload path to over 1 GW. The 116 MW planned figure reflects the executed first-phase ESA only; full buildout remains a projection. Investment: $6B stated without 'up to' qualifier across operator, MDA, and Governor's office sources; Governor's office describes it as the third-largest economic development project in Mississippi history. Jobs: 'at least 60 direct, high-tech jobs' and 'hundreds of indirect jobs ranging from construction to other related industries' — projections, not firm figures; no construction vs permanent breakdown confirmed. Rooftop solar of 20+ MW planned (behind-the-meter). Recycled water and new sewer line extension cited by operator as water infrastructure options. Estimated $23M in ad valorem tax revenue annually per Rankin First (county economic development group). Coordinates approximate (Brandon city center, Rankin County).

properties.name: Amazon Web Services Bossier Parish Campus (Benton)
properties.notes: One of the two campuses covered by Amazon's $12 billion northwest Louisiana announcement; the other is just north of Blanchard Latex Road in Caddo Parish. KSLA places this campus about five miles north of Benton on the west side of Highway 3. STACK Infrastructure is the developer partner and each campus is approximately 2-3 million sq ft. Program-level figures are deliberately not attributed to this site: the $12 billion investment and the roughly 1,500 construction / 540 permanent job figures cover both campuses jointly, and Amazon's up-to-$400 million public water-infrastructure commitment covers all of its northwest Louisiana campuses. properties.name: Amazon Boardman Exascale Data Center Campus
properties.poweredBy: Oregon grid (majority hydro); local retail utility PacifiCorp (Pacific Power)
properties.notes: Amazon confirmed the land purchase ($37M per Morrow County property records, confirmed by multiple news sources) but stated development plans are not final. Planning documents submitted to Morrow County describe a 1 GW exascale campus with 20 buildings across 4 million sq ft; Johnson Economics estimated $8B-$12B total investment. Land previously owned by Threemile Canyon Farms dairy. Distinct from Amazon's existing ~800 acres of operating/under-construction OR facilities. Lincoln Chronicle source URL returned 403 on fetch — primary claim supported by DCD source. energy.utility corrected from 'Bonneville Power Administration' (wholesale) to 'PacifiCorp (Pacific Power)' (retail utility). Coordinates are Boardman city centroid; exact site not publicly confirmed. Johnson Economics' economic-impact analysis (Morrow County Planning Commission, Jan 2025) models the full 1 GW campus at roughly $8 billion investment (potential range $7-12 billion), about 6,400 construction FTE over an eight-year build (~800/year) and about 560 operations FTE, assuming an Oregon Strategic Investment Program (SIP) property-tax abatement — modeled projections for a still-proposed campus, not firm commitments.

properties.name: AWS Project Green Campus
properties.notes: Codename 'Project Green'; application filed via NorthPoint Development, LLC. Two-phase build-out: Phase 1 = 8 data center buildings; Phase 2 = 13 additional buildings (21 total). Located on ~1,000 acres at northeast quadrant of I-70 and Highway 19 interchange near New Florence. Official AWS/Governor Kehoe announcement on June 15, 2026 cited a $10B investment commitment. Earlier county planning documents and initial filings referenced a maximum capital investment ceiling of up to $35B — that figure is a speculative ceiling, not a committed amount. AWS separately announced a 138MW renewable energy project in Missouri; not confirmed as dedicated to this campus. Community investments included in announcement: $3M for county 911/emergency dispatch upgrades, $3M for community programs, $1M for Montgomery County Fairgrounds, $150K community fund, $50K teacher grant. Preserve Montgomery County LLC filed suit in February 2026 alleging ten counts of Missouri Sunshine Law violations (closed-session negotiations, NDAs with Amazon); case pending as of mid-2026. First buildings targeted operational by 2027; full campus potentially complete ~2032. Coordinates are approximate (parcel centroid at I-70 / Hwy 19 NE quadrant). Jobs: KOMU reported ~400 permanent jobs; DCD's coverage of the same $10B announcement cited no specific permanent figure (only 'thousands of construction jobs') — permanent count left unstructured pending firm corroboration.

properties.name: Project Blue
properties.notes: Unincorporated Pima County, west of Houghton Rd, near Tucson. 500-700MW planned across 13M sq ft (a range, so omitted from capacityMw). AWS confirmed as end-customer via an NDA obtained by AZ Luminaria. Distinct site from Beale Infrastructure's Fremont Peak Properties/Luckett Road project in the Town of Marana (also AZ, also tracked this session) - same developer family, different parcel. Coordinates are approximate. The 180 permanent jobs figure is a projection for the third year of operations in 2029, published by Pima County and by the developer. Beale's own letter of 2025-09-17 adds a qualifier the county FAQ omits: the figure "include[s] full-time contractors and support personnel", and at least 75 of the roles will be directly employed by the end user. Beale has also stated it "is not asking for property tax incentives, often a necessary component of a data center project's cost competitiveness", and the utility agreement with Tucson Electric Power carries no financial incentives or discounts — unusual for a project of this size, and the reason subsidies are recorded as absent rather than merely unsearched.

properties.name: Beltline Energy Oklahoma City Campus
properties.notes: Two adjoining parcels rezoned via PUD cases likely numbered PUD-2105 (111.5 acres at 3025 N. Frisco Road, near I-40/Frisco Rd) and PUD-2124 (184 acres at 13921 NW 23rd Street, near NW 23rd/Frisco Rd, ~0.5 mi west of Yukon) — the case-number-to-address pairing is probable (inferred by matching geographic descriptors across sources) but not confirmed by a single primary document naming both together. OKC Planning Commission voted 7-0 to recommend approval Jan 21 2026; City Council final vote status is unconfirmed as of this writing (okc.gov council agendas were inaccessible during research) — treat as still-pending, not approved. Explicitly carved out of OKC's citywide data-center moratorium (~April 2026) as an already-pending application, confirming it remains active. Press coverage separately cites a larger '350-acre' and '480-acre' project total that doesn't reconcile with the confirmed 295.5-acre rezoned total (111.5+184) — the gap is plausibly an adjacent ~184.5-acre parcel Yukon Municipal Authority sold to BLE Landholdings LLC for $15.8M in Aug 2025 (near Hwy 66/Frisco Rd), which may be the same tract as the NW 23rd St parcel, but this is not confirmed. A $1B investment / 0.5GW capacity figure is associated with the broader Yukon-area BLE deal in local reporting but was not found tied specifically to this OKC rezoning by a primary source — omitted from capacityMw/investmentUsd pending confirmation rather than asserted.

Classified data_center (mid-conversion to AI), consistent with the tracked Bitdeer Knoxville TN conversion. Coordinates approximate (Pangborn area, Douglas County). Distinct from Bitdeer's tracked Ohio (Massillon/Clarington/Niles/Shalersville), Texas (Rockdale) and Tennessee (Knoxville) sites.

properties.name: Bloomberg LP Data Center
properties.notes: 155 Corporate Drive, Orangeburg, NY (Town of Orangetown, Rockland County). 131,805 sq ft total, two data halls totaling 39,058 sq ft with 42" raised floor and 26' clear height, 4.0 MW power system, 1,200-ton cooling capacity — all per an authoritative SEC EDGAR CMBS filing (2014). Construction cost was $123.2M ($935/sq ft) per that same filing, with Bloomberg contributing $39.0M toward construction; recorded here as investmentUsd rather than the frequently-cited $710M figure, which represents total lease payments over a 15-year term (expiring March 2029), not construction capital — those are not comparable numbers and conflating them would overstate the capital investment. Dedicated single-tenant enterprise facility built to Bloomberg's spec for its financial data/analytics terminals (not shared colocation), built/topped-off 2013-2014. No expansions since 2014 were found in this research pass, but absence of news is not proof of none. Coordinates are a town-level geocode, not a confirmed parcel pin.

properties.name: Cipher Black Pearl Campus
properties.notes: ~300 gross MW HPC/AI campus near Wink, Winkler County, under a 15-year AWS lease; Phase I targeted Q4 2026. Cipher transitioning crypto → HPC/AI. Coordinates are the Wink area centroid. Cipher Mining (Nasdaq: CIFR) financed Black Pearl via ~$2.0B senior secured notes (Black Pearl Compute LLC, Feb 2026) plus a ~$232.5M equity reimbursement (~$2.23B implied total, inferred across two instruments) -> investmentUsd omitted; the ~$9.3-9.8B AWS figure is 15-year lease revenue, not capex. No jobs figures disclosed -> jobs honest-zero. Mining-era cooling was ~250 MW air-cooled + ~50 MW liquid-cooled; the HPC/AI cooling architecture is undisclosed -> water honest-zero. No confirmed public subsidy surfaced. Cipher Mining was renamed Cipher Digital.

properties.name: CloudBurst San Marcos GigaCenter
properties.poweredBy: On-site natural gas (Energy Transfer Oasis Pipeline, up to 1.2 GW behind-the-meter)
properties.notes: 706-acre campus spanning Hays and Guadalupe counties; coordinates use San Marcos city area as centroid. Developed with Evolve Holdings as construction manager. 10-12 hyperscale buildings totaling ~3 million sq ft planned. Tenant not publicly confirmed. properties.name: Coachella Valley Technology Campus
properties.notes: 450-acre, two-phase project (Phase 1: 240 acres, reportedly 270-300 MW across three to six buildings - sources disagree on the building count; Phase 2: 210 acres, up to roughly 600 MW combined) near the Fillmore Street and Avenue 52 intersection in eastern Coachella. Status recorded as cancelled as the closest schema fit: the city's only concrete agreement with the developer was terminated by City Council on 2026-06-04 and the city is one to two votes (2026-08-12, 2026-08-26) from a permanent data-center ban, though the developer has not formally withdrawn. Re-check after the August 2026 council votes. No AI/HPC-specific marketing found anywhere - both the developer and press use generic 'data center'/'technology campus' language; the NBC headline's 'AI data center' phrasing is journalistic shorthand, not developer marketing. Planned around three microgrids and an energy center under a self-supplied municipal-utility model (Coachella Valley Power Services LLC, a Stronghold subsidiary; DMK Project Solutions Services is the named project-management partner); the Imperial Irrigation District separately projected approximately $42M in municipal-utility infrastructure financing - not project capex, so investmentUsd is left unset. Capacity is disclosed only as a range and jobs only as vague estimates ('hundreds of local jobs'), so both are omitted from structured fields per this dataset's range-omit convention. Only cross-streets are known (Fillmore Street and Avenue 52) - no parcel address confirmed. Coordinates are an approximate road-segment geocode (Avenue 52), not a parcel-confirmed point.

properties.name: Cologix COL5
properties.notes: Address 6787 Green Meadows Drive, Lewis Center OH 43035, southeast corner of Green Meadows Drive and Home Road, Orange Township. Power to be supplied by AEP. Phase 1 (135,000 sq ft, 25MW) construction began June 2025, targeted completion fall 2026; may expand to 75MW. Received 50%/10-year Ohio sales tax exemption (~$42.3M combined with the Licking County site) plus a 10-year 50% Delaware County property tax abatement, approved at the June 1, 2026 Ohio Tax Credit Authority meeting — the last such approval before Gov. DeWine's announced pause on new data center tax breaks. Coordinates are the Lewis Center/Orange Township town centroid, not parcel-verified in this session — recommend a follow-up parcel-level geocode of 6787 Green Meadows Drive before publishing at high precision.

properties.name: CoreWeave Dalton II / Core Scientific Old Tilton Road Data Center
properties.notes: Whitfield County BOC rezoning (3-2, tie broken by Chairman Jevin Jensen) approved March 2025 for 'heavy manufacturing' use (AI data center per contemporaneous reporting), conditioned on Enterprise Drive access. A June 2026 Whitfield Superior Court validated a $1.2B Integra SPV equipment-bond package tied to this ~167-173 acre site, naming CoreWeave Dalton II LLC as sublessee/operator. Same June 2026 hearing validated much larger CoreWeave Dalton / CoreWeave Dalton II bond series ($900M + $6.4B + $6.7B) that likely cover Core Scientific's OTHER Whitfield campus sites (Industrial South Road, Enterprise Drive) — those are separate parcels/rezonings and were not pursued as additional candidates this pass to avoid parcel-level double-counting; flagged for a future lane pass with GIS/parcel-level dedup once individual site addresses for those bond packages are confirmed. Core Scientific is site owner; CoreWeave Dalton II, LLC is sublessee/operator.

properties.name: Crusoe Warrenton Campus
properties.notes: Coordinates approximate. Site address: 22151 NW Service Road, Warrenton MO; north of NW Service Road, west of Hwy. W. Two 805,000 sq ft data center buildings + 40,000 sq ft administration building + 621,250 sq ft Ameren-owned switch yard + 603,200 sq ft Crusoe-owned electrical substation. Crusoe described as its 'fifth campus' in its national AI data center portfolio as of June 2026 per Crusoe newsroom. Meta signed agreement with Crusoe in June 2026 for approximately 1.6GW of AI computing capacity split across Childress TX and Warrenton MO campuses — per-site split not disclosed; confirms Warrenton as AI anchor customer site (sourceRef 3). Status: conditional use permit and site plan approved; land disturbance review and construction permits still outstanding before groundbreaking. Crusoe committed publicly to seek no real property tax or gross receipt tax abatements; would pursue state incentives only (sourceRef 2). Developer projected annual property taxes ~$80M/year (sourceRef 1), with ~$44M to local schools. Construction jobs projected ~2,000-2,500 over ~3-year build; permanent tech jobs projected ~100 (developer estimates, sourceRef 1 and 2 — not firm contractual commitments). Crusoe historically used on-site flared natural gas but divested those operations; Warrenton campus is grid-connected via Ameren Missouri — no on-site gas generation reported here. Distinct from the Google/Crusoe 'Goodnight' campus in Armstrong County TX.

properties.name: DC BLOX Atlanta East Hyperscale Data Center Campus
properties.notes: Coordinates approximate; physical address is 1726 Farmer Road NW, Conyers GA 30012. Land: 72 acres acquired per press release; Georgia EPD permit SAS-2024-00075 references 52.84-acre development footprint with three 40MW buildings. Capacity: 216MW total committed by Georgia Power per utility agreement and DRI filing; DC BLOX facility page cites 154 critical/IT MW (1 × 10MW + 3 × 48MW buildings = 154MW IT load). Dark fiber metro ring planned around Atlanta connecting Atlanta East and Atlanta West campuses and continuing to Myrtle Beach cable landing station. AI/ML applications explicitly cited in press materials as key driver of Atlanta hyperscale demand. DISTINCT from DC BLOX Atlanta West campus in Douglas County (Lithia Springs, ~55 acres, 180MW). Investment amount not publicly disclosed. Job counts not disclosed.

properties.name: DigiCo LAX1 (1977 Saturn Street)
properties.notes: DigiCo Infrastructure REIT is externally managed by HMC Capital (ASX-listed); the applicant/signing entity was HMC StratCap 1977 Saturn, LLC. Approximately 250,000 sq ft hyperscale data center campus planned at 1977 Saturn Street, adjacent to a companion site at 1980 Saturn Street (referred to in trade coverage as DigiCo 'LAX2') which is NOT tracked as a separate record here - LAX2's specifics trace only to aggregator listings with no independent primary or press confirmation found this pass; it is being divested in the same HMC Capital transaction. Capacity disputed, omitted: sources disagree materially (49.5-50 MW per Fox Business and No Data Center MPK, citing the applicant's own Initial Study/MND; approximately 56 MW per aggregators, apparently derived from 14 backup diesel generators at 4 MW each; 66-72 MW per CoStar describing 'the original proposal') and the primary withdrawal letter discloses no MW figure at all. Acreage disputed, omitted: approximately 5 acres per a community group's math from the building footprint versus 16 acres per Baxtel (aggregator-only - treated as unconfirmed). HMC Capital bought the parcel for approximately $39M (December 2024) and has agreed to sell it back for roughly $39M plus $33.5M for the adjacent LAX2 site plus a $10M contingent earn-out, settling in H1 FY27 - real-estate transaction values, not construction capex, since the facility was never built; investmentUsd is left unset. properties.name: Digital Realty Vernon Data Center
properties.notes: Raw industrial land (5.4 acres, with an existing 1925-era ~235,000-253,200 sq ft building to be redeveloped) purchased for $48.8M, closing November 4, 2025, from Pacific Santa Fe Industrial, LLC; Digital Realty's own Q3 2025 earnings release confirms ~5 acres/~$49M/32MW IT capacity for a Los Angeles-metro site. No AI/HPC-specific marketing found - this is undeveloped land with no announced tenant. Distinct from the already-tracked databank-vernon-la-ca (DataBank/Goodman Group JV) and from Prime Data Centers' operational LAX01 (4701 South Santa Fe Avenue) - trade coverage describing a Prime facility under construction 'across the street' likely refers to a Prime expansion phase near its original campus rather than the original LAX01 building itself. One of at least three independent Vernon data-center developments drawn by Vernon Public Utilities' below-market industrial power rates. Coordinates are an approximate street-level geocode, not a parcel-confirmed point.

"MCN" is EdgeConneX's internal project prefix (not publicly decoded). Distinct from EdgeConneX's separate Piper Farms parcel (~5 mi away) and from edgeconnex-ashville-oh (Pickaway County).

properties.name: Etheridge Lakes Data Center (Great Bridge)
properties.notes: 22.6-acre parcel on west side of Centerville Turnpike, south of Etheridge Manor Boulevard, Great Bridge area of Chesapeake. Developer Doug Fuller (Emerald Lakes Estates) sought rezoning from agricultural to light industrial; proposed 350,000 sq ft, 35 ft tall, 24/7 staffed facility. City Council denied the rezoning request unanimously. Separately, in July 2026 the Chesapeake Planning Commission recommended a citywide data-center zoning ordinance/policy (conditional use in industrial districts + Fentress Airfield Overlay only) — this is a POLICY change, not a site-specific candidate, and is not included here. No other active Chesapeake DC site rezoning was found this session. Coordinates are approximate (Centerville Turnpike/Great Bridge area); exact parcel not geocoded from GIS this session. Chesapeake City Council denied the rezoning 7-0 on 2025-06-17 (Planning Commission had recommended denial 6-1). Recorded as a cancelled proposal.

No AI/HPC-specific marketing found for this facility.

properties.name: Project Matador
properties.notes: 11GW is the long-term ceiling for the HyperGrid campus; near-term company targets include 1GW by end of 2026 and 2.3GW first-phase delivery — these are company goals, not firm commitments. Land acreage reported variously (5,769 acres per DCD July 2025 and 5,855 acres per other sources; later company materials cite 7,570 acres on 7,570 acres); using 5,769 as the earliest confirmed figure, sourced from the gas turbine acquisition announcement. Coordinates approximate (seed-provided; site in Carson County ~12 miles NE of Amarillo, adjacent to DOE Pantex Plant). Fermi America co-founded January 2025 by former Texas Governor and U.S. Energy Secretary Rick Perry, Toby Neugebauer (CEO, departed April 2026 after being fired 'without cause'), and Griffin Perry. IPO raised $682M on Nasdaq under ticker FRMI (October 2025), valuing company at ~$19B at opening; market cap collapsed to ~$3.4B by April 2026 after leadership exits and loss of anchor tenant ($150M LOI canceled December 2025). Company organized as a REIT; had zero revenue at IPO. Investment: equipment financing commitments exceed $600M ($500M MUFG turbine warehouse + $200M Keystone/Cape facility); projected total project cost $70–90B is a range/projection, not a firm figure — omitted from investmentUsd per data-rigor policy. Jobs: 50,000+ projected across campus lifetime — projection only, omitted from jobs field. Nuclear campus name in NRC COLA filings: 'President Donald J. Trump Advanced Energy and Intelligence Campus'; publicly marketed as Project Matador / HyperGrid.

properties.name: Flexential Parker (Compark)
properties.notes: 249,000 sq ft on 17 acres on Compark Boulevard near South Chambers Road. The town of Parker approved rezoning and a data center overlay district in February 2024 after a January 2024 planning-commission approval. A $19.3 million Douglas County business-personal-property tax rebate over 35 years was scheduled for a commissioner vote the week of 2026-08-11; it is not recorded here as a subsidy because the award had not been made as of the source date. County estimate of 16 permanent positions; company representatives suggested 30-50. Coordinates are an approximate Compark Boulevard geocode, not parcel-confirmed. Distinct from Flexential's existing Aurora, Centennial, Downtown and Englewood Denver-market sites.

properties.name: Goodnight Campus
properties.notes: Campus name: Goodnight, near the town of Claude, TX (known address: 10001 Lima Rd, Claude, TX 79019). Coordinates approximate (based on dispatch seed; county parcel area). Developed by Crusoe Energy via entity GN DC1, LLC (Delaware LLC, 255 Filmore St., Denver, CO 80206); Google is the hyperscale tenant/customer, confirmed publicly November 2025. Tax abatement agreement was signed with GN DC1, LLC in late 2024 without publicly naming the tenant. Google confirmed the Crusoe partnership but had not signed an offtake agreement for the on-site gas plant as of early 2026; negotiations on power amounts still ongoing per Google spokesperson. Planned IT capacity: Phase 1 described in tax abatement agreement as 'anticipated to consume up to 530 MW,' 4 buildings each with 4 x 25 MW data halls, on approximately 350 acres; Phase 2 (possible additional 3+ buildings) reported at up to ~500 MW additional; combined full build-out reported as 1 GW+ — all capacity figures are 'up to' ceilings from permit and abatement documents, not firm contracted amounts. Project was scaled back from an original 7-building plan (October 2025 local reporting); 4 buildings with construction permits from TDLR as of early 2026; Crusoe described 3-4 buildings as likely; grading on additional parcels suggests total program may reach 5+ buildings. First phase expected online 2026; initial county PILOT payment expected June/July 2026. The $40B Google Texas investment is a statewide commitment through 2027 covering multiple sites (Armstrong County, Haskell County, Ellis County) with no site-specific investment figure disclosed by Google. A $29B campus investment figure appeared in Aterio/Crusoe reporting — this is a projected ceiling, not a firm committed amount; omitted from investmentUsd per data-rigor policy. Distinct from Google's separate Haskell County TX site and Red Oak (Ellis County) TX sites — do not conflate. Building 3 is scheduled for completion 2026-08-01; Building 4 is due March 2027. Nothing at the campus is yet described as operational.

properties.name: Google Project BOSC (Lima)
properties.notes: Google's third Ohio data center (after New Albany and Lancaster). $500M confirmed capital investment. Codename Project BOSC; pre-announcement land/permit work via Bistrozzi LLC (Delaware shell). Coordinates are the Lima city centroid; the confirmed site is in American Township ~2 mi north of Lima (North Cole Street between Beery and Irvin Roads), ~170 acres. Capacity MW not disclosed. Google's project page states construction anticipated to begin late 2026; ~50 permanent jobs projected per DCD and 'hundreds' of construction jobs - projections, so omitted from jobs. Ohio EPA air-permit application (pending March 2026) covers 115 emergency diesel generators; 36 cooling towers specified. $50M of the investment is earmarked for local road infrastructure, $13.6M for water infrastructure.

properties.name: Google Haskell County Data Center Campus
properties.notes: Two data center buildings at one Haskell County site; treated as a single campus record. Announced Nov 14 2025 as part of Google's $40B Texas investment through 2027 (which also covers Armstrong County and a Wilbarger County/Vernon site); no Haskell-specific investment figure disclosed, so investmentUsd is omitted (the $40B is a Texas-wide aggregate). One building is co-located with the Quantum Clean Energy Project (Intersect Power, acquired by Google March 2026): 640 MW solar PV + 1.3 GWh battery storage, scheduled operational June 2026 - this is energy-project capacity, NOT data-center IT load. Job figures cited in press (1,200 construction / up to 11 permanent) come from the co-located Intersect energy project, not the data center, so they are noted here rather than in jobs. Coordinates are the Haskell city centroid (no parcel-level GPS found).

properties.notes: Google's FOURTH Nebraska site by official count and genuinely distinct from both Papillion (Sarpy Co.) and Omaha (Douglas Co.) -- also DISTINCT from the separate proposed Google/Tenaska gas-plant mega-campus already tracked as google-nebraska-ai-campus-proposed (that one is a ~4-county, still-undeveloped 1,000-3,000MW proposal; this one is Google's confirmed, currently-building third/fourth site in north Lincoln). properties.name: Google New Albany Data Center
properties.notes: 1101 Beech Rd SW, New Albany — operated via Google's Ohio subsidiary Montauk Innovations LLC. 275,000 sq ft initial building on a ~440-447 acre campus. $600M confirmed initial capital investment; 100% real-property tax abatement (15yr) and 100% sales-tax exemption (~$43.5M value, 15yr) granted. Distinct from Google's Lima "Project BOSC" facility (different county) and Google's Lancaster campus (tracked separately). No IT-load MW figure publicly disclosed. In June 2025, the same Montauk Innovations entity acquired an adjacent 85-acre parcel at 2565 Harrison Road NW (~4 miles north) for $63M; Google has NOT confirmed this parcel will become a data center ("we want to ensure we have the option to further grow, should our business demand it" per a spokesperson) — tracked as a note here rather than a standalone facility pending confirmation. No AI/HPC-specific marketing found — Google's own materials describe this and its other Ohio campuses generically as cloud/digital infrastructure. County-auditor parcels confirm the campus straddles the Franklin-Licking line: the operational, data-center-classed parcel is in Franklin County (5266 Babbitt Rd, 222 ac, Montauk Innovations LLC, acquired Dec 2018 for $27.4M), extending east across the line into Licking County at 1101 Beech Rd SW (219 ac; ~441 ac combined). The coordinate is now parcel-exact to the Franklin operational parcel.

properties.name: Google Project Louie (Morgan County)
properties.notes: Codename 'Project Louie'; Google initially concealed via shell company 'Woodland Caribou LLC'. Planned 1,200 MW AES Indiana substation per IURC Cause No. 46394 (filed Apr 22 2026); that figure is the utility substation capacity ceiling, not a confirmed steady-state data center load — treated as notes per spec. Land acquisition spend: ~$78 million for ~15 parcels Sep–Nov 2025. Coordinates approximate (site east of Monrovia near SR-42/Keller Hill Rd area). Annexation dispute with Town of Monrovia active July 2026: county transferred Google parcels to RDC under IC 36-4-3-4.3 to block annexation; Google offered $12M sewer plant upgrade to Monrovia to drop the effort.

properties.name: HostDime Orlando Tier IV Data Center
properties.notes: 5-acre parcel (of the historic 99-acre Hungerford tract) fronting I-4 at Wymore Rd -- governing municipality is Eatonville, not Maitland; HostDime's own current marketing copy lists a mailing address of "1 Innovative Pl, Maitland, FL 32751" while an aggregator (baxtel) lists "1000 Wymore Rd, Eatonville, FL" for the same building -- both addresses are disputed/unverifiable via parcel search, so no street field is recorded. 100,000 sq ft, 7-story building, 3 data-center floors, >1,000 racks. Groundbreaking May 2021; HostDime's own landing page and data-sheet page disagree on completion quarter (Q3 2026 vs Q2 2026) and the project has slipped repeatedly since an original ~2024 target; as of ClickOrlando's June 2026 report the facility was still not open. Investment is conflicting and stale: GrowthSpotter (Oct 2023) reported an original $35M budget grown to $58M actual (65.7% overrun); a separately-circulating $100M figure is single-sourced and unreconciled, so no investmentUsd is recorded. No disclosed capacityMw. Distinct from HostDime's unrelated, already-operational 25,000 sq ft Tier III facility at 440 W Kennedy Blvd, Orlando. Eatonville Town Council (led by Councilwoman Wanda Randolph) has pushed a transparency measure over electricity/water use, noise, and appearance, and has assessed missed-deadline fines ($250-500/day); this intersects Florida SB 484 (effective July 1, 2026), which expands local authority over large-load customers and data-center water permits.

properties.name: IREN Horizon — Childress, TX
properties.notes: SEPARATE SITE from IREN Sweetwater (Nolan/Fisher County — do not conflate). Full 750 MW figure is total campus transmission capacity; the AI/Microsoft Horizon 1–4 build-out comprises four 50 MW IT (75 MW gross) liquid-cooled data halls = 200 MW IT total, targeting end-2026 delivery. Horizon 1 (50 MW IT / 75 MW gross) energized Q4 2025 — operational; Horizons 2–4 remain under construction as of mid-2026. Coordinates approximate (county seat area). Site is a 576-acre freehold parcel with on-site 345 kV substations connecting directly to ERCOT. Investment for Horizon 1–4 reported as $300–350M (range; not a firm figure — omitted from investmentUsd). Microsoft contract ($9.7B total, 5-year through ~2031) covers NVIDIA GB300 Blackwell Ultra GPU cloud services; 20% upfront prepayment funded capex. Dell Technologies hardware supply agreement: $5.8B. IREN also holds a separate NVIDIA cloud services contract at Childress. Rack density 130–200 kW per rack; projected PUE 1.05–1.10. Approximately 25 current full-time local employees, 50+ expected at 750 MW full build-out; over 500 contractors during construction phase (approximate reported figures — omitted from jobs numeric fields). IREN Community Grants Program distributes $250,000 annually to the Childress area.

properties.name: IREN Sweetwater Campus
properties.notes: Two-site campus: Sweetwater 1 (1,400 MW, ~1,700 acres, Nolan/Jones County boundary area) substation energized May 1, 2026 via 345kV ERCOT connection; data centers commissioning in phases. Sweetwater 2 (600 MW, ~500 acres, Fisher County, near Hamlin TX, ~28 miles from SW1) targeted energization late 2027 per IREN (some sources cite 2028). Direct fiber loop planned between sites for single 2 GW compute hub with <10ms latency to Dallas. Coordinates are approximate (Sweetwater city center, Nolan County seat). County boundary sources conflicting: DCD says Fisher County for both sites; interconnection.fyi and dispatch brief cite Nolan County for SW1; northwiseproject.com says Nolan and Jones Counties span the campus. IREN's $9.7B Microsoft contract (Nov 2025) and $3.4B NVIDIA contract (May 2026) are company-wide deals currently deployed at Childress, TX campus (Horizon 1-4); the NVIDIA partnership press release specifically names Sweetwater as the flagship future deployment site for NVIDIA DSX factory architecture. No confirmed customer contracts specific to Sweetwater site as of 2026-07-07. IREN was in Sweetwater since 2022 as a Bitcoin mining site; HPC/AI pivot announced October 2024. Interconnection.fyi lists renewable energy sourcing via RECs (wind/solar) at this site.

properties.name: Lancium Clean Campus (Crusoe / Stargate Site 1)
properties.poweredBy: ERCOT grid; Crusoe has separately contracted 4.5 GW of natural gas supply for its broader multi-site AI buildout
properties.notes: Originally proposed Dec 2021 as Lancium's "Project Artemis" — a Bitcoin-mining and grid-demand-response campus using stranded/curtailed West Texas wind and solar power, with Lancium throttling load during ERCOT peak demand. Crusoe Energy has since built and operates AI/HPC data-center buildings on the site (publicly branded "Stargate Site 1"), with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure as the tenant hosting NVIDIA GPU clusters for OpenAI's Stargate project — Oracle sits contractually between Crusoe and OpenAI; no confirmed direct OpenAI-Crusoe lease. Lancium retains land/electrical-infrastructure ownership; Crusoe leases and operates part of an approximately 800-1,000-acre campus. First 2 of 8 planned buildings (~200+ MW) were operational by mid-2025; remaining 6 are under construction, with a full 1.2 GW build-out targeted for completion in 2026-2027 (dates vary by source). Construction-workforce and total AI-era investment figures conflict significantly across sources (reported range: 2,000-9,000 workers; an unverified ~$11.6B raise) and are not repeated here as fact. Coordinates are approximate (geocoded from a listed street address, not parcel-confirmed — the ~800-1,000-acre campus could place any specific building up to ~1-2 miles from this point). Also known as the Lancium Clean Campus.

properties.notes: Site scaled and moved twice: original Nov 2024 plan was ~15 acres/155,000 sq ft/~$15M/~15 MW at University Commerce Park; by fall 2025 it had grown to a 29.2-acre city-owned parcel at 1380 University Boulevard, 320,000 sq ft, 200+ MW, $1B+ (Wharton Equity Partners partnership). No AI/HPC-specific marketing language found in any source, so aiClassification is omitted. Coordinates are the Hamilton, OH city-area centroid, not an independently geocoded parcel point for 1380 University Boulevard.

Coordinates approximate the street address.

properties.name: Manse Technology Campus
properties.notes: Formerly referred to as Project Blackjack; sited on the Manse Road corridor near the southern entrance to Pahrump along Highway 160, roughly 1,100 feet from the nearest homes. Developer states $18.4 billion of capital investment at full buildout and $114 million in annual Nye County property taxes; a separate figure of $8.4 billion appeared in other reporting and was not resolved this session, so the developer's own $18.4B is recorded. Design features include screening berms, rooftop parapets for sound reduction and a target of roughly 55 dB at the property line. No megawatt capacity has been disclosed. Construction is anticipated to begin in 2027 with a five-year buildout, pending approvals that the county moratorium currently blocks.

properties.name: Markley Group One Lowell Data Center
properties.notes: Coordinates are approximate city centroid (Sacred Heart/Back Central neighborhoods, Lowell). Facility serves 100+ customers including hospitals, universities, and police departments. Expansion includes land purchases by Markley near old power plant. Expansion plans stalled by moratorium. AI demand cited as driver of expansion since 2022. Delivered permanent-job counts are disputed - the abatement promised 100 jobs; the city and critics count ~26-30 full-time local workers while Markley cites ~100 total, with construction peaking ~120 (IBEW Local 103); recorded as unresolved (honest-zero). No confirmed total capital-investment figure is public ('hundreds of millions'). Massachusetts' 2024 sales-tax exemption is statutory eligibility, not a confirmed Markley award.

properties.notes: End operator undisclosed behind Balloonist LLC (a Delaware foreign LLC). properties.name: Meta Project Anthem — Tulsa
properties.notes: Codename: Project Anthem (used in TMAPC filings; Meta confirmed publicly April 21, 2026). Meta's 28th US data center and 32nd globally; first in Oklahoma and first built within Tulsa city limits. Anchor tenant at Fair Oaks Innovation Park (a 2,000-acre campus) near 11th Street and Creek Turnpike, East Tulsa. Investment stated as 'more than $1 billion' by Meta — a floor figure only; PartnerTulsa estimates construction costs at ~$800M. investmentUsd omitted: no firm single confirmed figure. Facility size: 2+ million sq ft; completion targeted 2028; general contractor Fortis Construction. No facility-specific MW capacity disclosed; Meta separately adding 1,500+ MW of clean energy to the Oklahoma grid statewide. Jobs: Meta states 'more than 1,000 construction workers at peak' and 'approximately 100 permanent jobs' — approximations from press release, not firm figures; omitted from numeric fields. Phase 2 expansion (375 additional acres west of original parcel, developer Atmoss LLC) proposed but withdrawn March 2026 before city council vote. Coordinates approximate (near 11th St & Creek Turnpike, East Tulsa).

properties.name: Meta Davenport Data Center
properties.notes: 328-acre parcel at the northwest corner of Hillandale Road and Enterprise Way in northwest Davenport, held through Vemerald LLC, described in a state news release as a wholly owned subsidiary of Meta Platforms, Inc. State board documents from May 2024 said Meta would evaluate the parcel until Q1 2025, break ground by Q4 2025 and complete the data center by end of 2027. As of March 2026 the land had been purchased but construction had not started, so status is held at proposed rather than under_construction. Job count is 35 at $28.76/hour or more per state board documents; Davenport city documents put it at 50. Distinct site from the tracked Meta Altoona campus.

properties.name: Meta Huntsville Data Center Campus
properties.notes: Address: 5400 Prosperity Dr NW, Huntsville, AL. Coordinates are approximate for Cummings Research Park area. Original 2.5M sq ft campus operational; expansion to 3.5M sq ft paused December 2022 for AI architecture redesign; Meta stated no intent to abandon site. Over 85 grants and $4.2M in sponsorships to Huntsville-area schools since 2019. Meta's stated investment rose to more than $1.5B with the June 2022 expansion (original 2018 build ~$750M); the 3.5M-sq-ft expansion was later paused for AI redesign, so the ultimately realized figure is uncertain. properties.name: Metrobloks Southfield Data Center
properties.notes: 217,030-230,000 sq ft, two-story building on ~12.19 acres of vacant land along Inkster Road north of 11 Mile Road, Southfield's northwest corner. Los Angeles-based developer Metrobloks (already tracked elsewhere in MO/IN/FL) has not completed a data center build anywhere yet per reporting. City of Southfield's own statement explicitly says the facility is NOT intended as 'an artificial intelligence repository' -- omitting aiClassification here rather than defaulting to 'likely'. City Council approved the site plan 5-2 on Dec 16, 2025; the city notes 'Approval of the proposal does not remove City oversight' -- still subject to further permitting. A named IT-engineer public commenter said the real target may be closer to 150 MW by groundbreaking; unconfirmed beyond that public comment. Closed-loop cooling planned, city says 'minimal long-term water use.' Coordinates are an approximate Inkster/11 Mile intersection estimate, not parcel-geocoded.

properties.name: Microsoft Fairwater Atlanta (Azure AI Superfactory)
properties.notes: 615-acre, up-to-13-building QTS-built campus on Hwy 54W near Fayetteville, Fayette County (Microsoft's materials say 'Atlanta'). Began operation Oct 2025 as Fairwater 2 — a 'multi-gigawatt' AI campus. ~1,500 MW is the anticipated ultimate Georgia Power load across all buildings (planned figure; ~433 MW cited as initially online). properties.name: Microsoft Data Center Campus – Rome, GA
properties.notes: Investment described as '$1 billion' in RFCDA announcement; Data Center Dynamics and Business Facilities use 'more than $1 billion' framing — treated as a floor, not a firm single figure (investmentUsd omitted per data policy). Completion targeted 2027–2028. Site is 347 acres on Huffaker Road, east of Fouche Gap Road, in unincorporated Floyd County, adjacent to Georgia Power-owned land; land purchased at $40,000/acre (~$13.9M). Microsoft stated site selection was driven by 'Rome and Floyd County's industrial zoning and strong infrastructure.' Microsoft committed to covering all costs for additional infrastructure (power, water, roads) so ratepayers and taxpayers are not burdened. Part of Microsoft's broader East US 3 Georgia cloud build-out; announced to bolster Azure cloud services. Floyd County enacted an 80-day moratorium on new data center permits (2025) but explicitly noted previously filed projects including Microsoft's can proceed. Capacity MW not disclosed. Coordinates are approximate; actual parcel is on Huffaker Road in unincorporated Floyd County.

properties.notes: Proposed ~$1B hyperscale campus at Covenant Business Park, Lowell Township, outside Grand Rapids. Originally filed under Franklin Lowell LLC / Franklin Partners (that application was withdrawn in Dec 2025 amid opposition); Microsoft has since publicly identified itself as the developer (named itself Jan 2026 per secondary reporting, not independently re-confirmed this session) and is pursuing a revamped proposal. properties.name: Microsoft Malaga Campus
properties.notes: Three-building campus at 5375 Malaga Alcoa Highway; two additional buildings possible by 2027 on demand. 288 MW figure from secondary aggregator Cleanview only; primary sources (DCD, Microsoft) do not specify MW capacity. Construction of first building began June 2023 per Microsoft Local blog; original statusHistory incorrectly dated under_construction to 2024-05. Expected operational 2026. Coordinates approximate for Malaga area on Malaga Alcoa Highway. A Building-1 permit cites ~72 peak-shift staff (a single-building figure, not a facility employment total); no confirmed total campus capital-expenditure figure is public. Go-live check 2026-08-08: NO citable operational date exists. Microsoft's own Malaga project page gives a first-phase construction window concluding in early 2026 but states plainly that "Completion of construction does not indicate datacenter operation/availability", and publishes no energization or service date. Secondary reporting that the first building would be "powered in August and fully operational by late 2026" is forward-looking and was not used to move the status. Remains under_construction. Microsoft's own Quincy/Central Washington community page states it "operates datacenters in Quincy and is developing new datacenters in Malaga and East Wenatchee" — positively confirming the site is not yet operational.

properties.name: Nebius Vineland Data Center
properties.notes: Phase-1 (~100 MW) completed summer 2025 in approximately 20 weeks from March 2025 announcement; full campus buildout targeting November 2026. Total design capacity cited as 'up to 300 MW' in Nebius press releases (sourceRef 0); DataOne CEO and local/community coverage consistently cite 350 MW; long-term campus potential described as approaching 1 GW. Coordinates are approximate (site: South Lincoln and Sheridan Avenues, East Vineland; Baxtel lists 805 Sheridan Ave). DataOne is the developer/builder — BSO's data center unit (launched 2024) backed by Ardian; CEO Charles-Antoine Beyney; this is DataOne's first US site (previously Grenoble and Lyon, France). Nebius is the ~10-year tenant; Microsoft GPU infrastructure agreement commencing late 2025 under multi-year AI infrastructure deal. Facility is 100% privately funded; DataOne declined a $6.2M city equipment loan amid community backlash. Distinct from Nebius's Independence, MO (Kansas City) site. NJDEP air permit pending as of early 2026; construction proceeded ahead of final permit issuance. DataOne stated 200+ permanent full-time jobs; construction job count not disclosed.

properties.name: PORTS-Pike Technology Campus
properties.notes: Officially "PORTS-Pike Technology Campus"; formerly tracked under the pre-announcement Ohio entity New Day Data Centers LLC, a name that appears nowhere in the SEC S-1 or SB Energy’s own announcements. Developer/operator is SB Energy (SoftBank-controlled); the DOE lease was signed 2026-02-26 by its subsidiary Pike County Portsmouth DC LLC. CAPACITY - three distinct figures that must not be conflated: 8.0 GW-IT of contracted compute (8,024 MW-IT; NVIDIA guarantees the initial 4.25 GW-IT with an option on the remaining 3.78 GW-IT), 10 GW of gross power load (the capacityMw.planned value here), and 9.2 GW of new gas generation. OFFTAKE: on 2026-08-17 SB Energy subsidiaries signed 17 twenty-year triple-net leases with OpenAI, with rent commencement conditioned on interconnection and generation being available; NVIDIA provided a residual-value guaranty capped at $105B and separately bought $1.5B of non-voting stock. LAND: landAcres is intentionally omitted - the DOE lease covers 189 acres (Batch 1) on which "one data center building is expected to be constructed", while the S-1 places the buildings "across several thousand acres of private property"; the widely-cited 3,700/3,777 acres is the whole federal reservation, which also hosts the separately tracked Oklo Aurora project, Centrus and the DUF6 plant. INVESTMENT: investmentUsd intentionally omitted - $10B (DOE, March) and $30-40B (project site) describe the same ~800 MW first phase and cannot both be right, the $67.2B total appears only as one trade outlet’s unattributed rollup, and the S-1 states no total capex. SUBSIDIES: none awarded - the Ohio Tax Credit Authority minutes record no award, no JobsOhio award was found, and Ohio paused new data-centre tax exemptions in May 2026; a county PILOT is under negotiation because the leased federal land yields no property tax. STATUS: early civil works began after the 2026-03-20 groundbreaking, though the S-1 lists construction as not started, with first capacity in 2028 and full buildout 2032. Distinct from oklo-aurora-pike-county-oh on the same broader site - do not merge or double-count.

properties.name: NTT Global Data Centers Mesa — Pacific Proving Technology Park
properties.notes: investmentUsd is $300M land purchase only; total buildout investment is substantially higher. NE corner of Pecos and Crismon roads, far SE Mesa. Seven two-story buildings totaling 1.7M sq ft + warehouse + office. NTT's second Phoenix-area campus (existing 102-acre, 240MW campus is ~4 miles north on Elliot Road). Phase 1 targeted November 2028. Coordinates approximate for Pecos/Crismon intersection. Status refresh 2026-08-08: the Planning & Zoning Board recommended approval 4-0 in mid-May 2026; the article (updated 2026-06-08) said the proposal "will likely be heard in late July or mid-August by council". No fetched source records a Council vote, so the status stays "proposed" — the 2026-07-20 date carried in earlier notes was an expected hearing date, not a decision.

properties.name: Oakland University Campus Computing Facility
properties.notes: Proposed shared university/industry colocation facility on OU's campus (Auburn Hills/Rochester border); site shifted from Parking Lot 35 to Parking Lot 37 to increase distance from a campus hall, a nature preserve, and a Native American heritage site. Cleveland-based Fairmount Properties funds construction, operations, and eventual decommissioning; OU pays nothing and gains an 8x expansion of its own computing capacity. Board of Trustees voted 7-0-1 to proceed into due diligence, design, and construction phases (June 2026); published timeline has due diligence running Oct 2026-June 2027, design July 2027-Fall 2028. Coordinates are an approximate campus-area estimate, not parcel-geocoded.

properties.name: Pierce County Energy Center
properties.notes: 420 MW solar array plus a 170 MW / four-hour-duration (680 MWh) battery storage system on 2,230 acres in rural Pierce County, northeast Nebraska (northwest of Norfolk), owned and operated by a subsidiary of NextEra Energy Resources. Built under a procurement framework in which Google supplies carbon-free energy resources to OPPD and shares the capacity attributes and cost savings with OPPD's wider customer base — the resource serves BOTH OPPD customers and Google, so it is NOT a behind-the-meter dedicated plant. Supports Google's 24/7-carbon-free-energy-by-2030 goal. OPPD reports $316.4 million of construction-phase economic impact and 542 construction jobs, then $5.7 million of annual business activity, 9 sustained jobs and over $2 million in local tax revenue once operating; Google's own post gives slightly different figures (540 construction jobs, $5.3 million annual economic activity over a 20-year life). The OPPD figures are used here and the discrepancy is left visible rather than averaged. capacityMw.planned carries the 420 MW solar figure only; the battery is storage, not generation, and is not double-counted. Coordinates are a rural-Pierce-County approximation, NOT a parcel-level geocode. Already named in the poweredBy field of google-papillion-ne but never tracked as its own facility.

properties.name: Turtle Creek Station
properties.notes: OPPD natural-gas peaking station near South 168th Street and Fairview Road in Sarpy County — the same county as the Meta Sarpy and Google Papillion campuses. Two Siemens Energy dual-fuel combustion turbines totalling 450 MW entered service in June 2025, each able to reach full output in under 11 minutes; a third 225 MW unit is under construction with completion targeted by end of 2028, taking the station to roughly 675 MW. Dual-fuel on natural gas with light fuel oil backup, and stated to be future-compatible with a 30% hydrogen/natural-gas blend or biodiesel. ⚠️ SCOPE CAVEAT FOR THE REVIEWER: NO source fetched this session names data centers as the driver for this plant. OPPD attributes it to 'significant growth in energy demand' and its Power with Purpose initiative, and separately states it expects to add load at 100 MW per year for the next 5-6 years — but the August 2025 board update explicitly does not identify what generates that growth. This record is offered on the same basis as the dataset's existing utility-plant entries with no named compute offtaker (aps-desert-sun-power-plant-gila-bend-az, dominion-chesterfield-energy-reliability-center-va); if the project's bar is a sourced compute nexus, REJECT this candidate. Coordinates are derived from the stated intersection, NOT a parcel geocode.

Investment amount, job figures, and water draw not disclosed in any sourced press materials. Joint venture: American Real Estate Partners (AREP) and Harrison Street.

properties.name: Prime Data Centers LAX01
properties.notes: Opened November 14, 2024; 33MW of critical IT power at full build-out across six data halls, 100% leased at opening to two initially-unnamed AI companies. Lambda was named as a tenant via a separate press release approximately one year later (November 13, 2025), leasing 21MW of the 33MW total for NVIDIA Blackwell-based AI infrastructure - these are two distinct announcements, not one event. One of at least three independent data-center developments in Vernon (a small, ~200-resident, all-industrial city), alongside a separate Digital Realty land purchase (4400 Pacific Blvd) and the DataBank/Goodman Group 'Vernon LA Campus' - driven by Vernon Public Utilities offering industrial power at roughly half the rate of neighboring investor-owned utilities.

properties.name: Project Hazelnut
properties.notes: Site: Humboldt North Industrial Park, Hazle Township, Luzerne County PA (within a larger ~3,000-acre industrial park); a few miles from Amazon's nuclear-adjacent data center campus (acquired from Talen Energy) - proximity only, AWS is NOT a confirmed tenant/operator for Project Hazelnut; NorthPoint's own project site names no end-tenant, describing this as a speculative build. Phased: Phase 1 (5 buildings) to begin Q4 2026, Phase 2 (3 buildings) Q1 2028, Phase 3 (7 buildings) Q2 2029. Developer projects ~900-1,300 construction jobs and ~900-950 permanent jobs ($50K-$158K salary range) - not yet delivered, so omitted from the jobs field; similarly $13.47M in projected county tax revenue over 20 years is a projection, not a subsidy. First surfaced publicly in connection with PA's Permit Fast Track Program (Executive Order 2024-04). NorthPoint's own site explicitly frames this as a general 'data center campus' supporting 'cloud platforms, digital payments, streaming, and healthcare systems' - no AI-specific language found; classified 'mixed_use' given hyperscale-tier campus scale makes AI workloads plausible even absent explicit branding.

properties.name: Prologis STEM Park
properties.notes: 159-acre city-owned parcel at Hwy 237 & Zanker Road, North San Jose (bounded by Los Esteros Energy Center, Artesian Slough, Hwy 237, and the Silicon Valley Advanced Water Purification Center). Prologis selected as preferred developer by San Jose City Council (unanimous vote, Nov 18 2025) over Catellus-Deca and Trammell Crow proposals; CEQA review and ground-lease negotiation still pending as of source dates — not yet approved. 'STEM Park' = Sustainable Technology, Engineering and Manufacturing Park: four 99MW data-center buildings (1.68M sq ft total, capacityMw above) plus a separate ~785,000 sq ft / 100MW advanced-manufacturing component (not counted in capacityMw, different use). PG&E has committed initial 250MW via dual feed from the Los Esteros 230kV substation within 30-36 months. ~$25B investment widely reported (DCD et al.) but not confirmed directly by Prologis — omitted from investmentUsd. Projected 6,000+ jobs and $30M/yr city tax revenue are projections tied to a not-yet-approved project, not delivered counts — omitted from jobs numeric. A separate, already-tracked Prologis site (prologis-silver-creek-valley-san-jose-ca) and another new Prologis San Jose site (prologis-rue-ferrari-san-jose-ca, this same batch) are distinct parcels, not duplicates.

properties.name: Antelope Data Center (Project Antelope)
properties.notes: West of Cedar City along Antelope Springs Road; permit deemed vested ahead of the county's 180-day data center moratorium; development planned in phases over 8-10 years; up to 6.75M sq ft at full buildout. Subsidies checked at the municipal tier (2026-09-04): no site-level subsidy. Iron County Planning Commission minutes for the 4 June 2026 conditional-use approval state "This CUP is not tied to any tax incentives or reimbursements", and no Iron County community-reinvestment project area was found covering this site, which lies in unincorporated Iron County outside Cedar City's municipal limits. The applicant's consultant told the commission their tax-revenue estimate was modelled both "with the Inland Port incentives and without", which is a future incentive being contemplated by the developer, not an awarded one.

properties.name: QTS Bessemer (Project Marvel)
properties.notes: Codename: Project Marvel. 18-building hyperscale campus on Red Ridge near I-459 and I-20/59 interchange in Bessemer (Jefferson County). Announced capacity: up to 1,200 MW at full build-out — reported as a planned ceiling, roughly 9% of Alabama Power's current generating capacity; recorded as capacityMw.planned = 1200 (an announced 'up to' full-build-out ceiling, consistent with how the dataset records other announced full-build-out figures). Investment: reported at $14–14.5B across sources (Logistics Land Investment anticipated 'close to $14.4B'; WBRC reported $14.5B at November 2025 rezoning; DCD reported ~$14B); no single firm company-confirmed figure exists — treated as a projected cost range and excluded from investmentUsd. Land: ~1,607.42 acres total after two rezoning rounds (initial ~700 acres November 2025 + 914-acre expansion April 2026). QTS affiliate purchased land from TPA Group affiliate for $431.73M. Chapter 9B statutory eligibility would have provided a 30-year abatement estimated at $500M+; QTS committed not to seek local property tax incentives (per WBRC July 2026) — subsidy excluded as eligibility does not equal award and QTS renounced pursuit. Full buildout timeline: 7+ years. Birmingham Business Alliance estimated ~$4B net benefit over 30 years; Bessemer City Schools projected ~$25M/year. AI framing not officially confirmed by QTS or the city as of July 2026 — size and scale (hyperscale, cloud/AI demand framing in QTS statement) support 'likely' classification. Coordinates are approximate for the Red Ridge parcel area. Jobs: ~1,000 construction and ~330 permanent are projected figures for the proposed (not-yet-built) campus (WBRC, Nov 2025) — recorded as projections in notes, not structured jobs fields, per data-rigor policy. QTS Data Centers is owned by Blackstone (2021 take-private).

properties.name: Rattlesnake Creek Wind Project
properties.notes: 320 MW / 101-turbine wind farm in Dixon County, northeast Nebraska, between the towns of Allen, Emerson and Wakefield — about 100 miles from the data center it serves. Built by Enel Green Power with $430 million of local investment; generates around 1,300 GWh/year, avoiding a reported 940,000 tons of CO2 annually. Enel's own project page states the plant powers Facebook's (Meta's) Sarpy data center — the named generation behind the '100% renewable' claim on meta-sarpy-springfield-ne, whose notes reference 'a wind farm in Dixon County' without naming it. Meta's own Sarpy info sheet independently states 'A Meta-supported project is adding 320 megawatts of new renewable energy in Nebraska', matching this project's nameplate exactly. Facebook's initial contracted share was 200 MW of the 320 MW, with the remaining 120 MW to other buyers and Adobe holding a 10 MW slice; Facebook was reported to take the full output over time. Originally conceived by Kansas-based Tradewind Energy in 2013. This is a contracted PPA resource on the grid, NOT behind-the-meter generation. Coordinates are an approximate centroid of the Allen/Emerson/Wakefield project area, NOT a turbine-array geocode. CAVEAT on 'primary is not current': the operator field records Enel Green Power as stated on the project's own live page fetched this session; Enel's US renewables portfolio has been subject to divestment activity industry-wide, so present ownership should be re-verified before publishing.

properties.name: RB Inyokern Data Center
properties.notes: Unincorporated Kern County site south of West Inyokern Road (Hwy 178) and west of North Brown Road (APNs 084-010-43, -44, -45 portion; broader ~95-acre study area across 19 APNs). The CEC SPPE docket formally governs 40 diesel backup generator sets rated to 99 MW combined backup capacity, described by the CEC as not electrically interconnected to the transmission or distribution grid; primary power is a separate 115 kV interconnection to Southern California Edison. Proposer entities per the primary CEC filing: Intuva Inc. and Valley Wide Engineering & Construction, alongside applicant R&L Capital, Inc. (CEO Robbie Barker). Unconfirmed pending a direct read of the CEC Basis-of-Design filing: press claims of '6 modular data halls' and on-site canopy solar. Jobs figures are inconsistent across sources (30-60 permanent, 1,600 temporary construction, and a softer 530-total-including-indirect claim, all secondary/company-sourced) and are omitted from the structured jobs field for that reason. Investment (~$250M) is a company estimate reported by Tehachapi News, not seen in a primary filing. A Phase I cultural resources survey found no CRHR-eligible or tribal cultural resources (NAHC response negative, 2026-03-16). Distinct from the already-tracked Golden Valley Technology Hub (Beacon/CRC, Elk Hills) - different operator, site, capacity, and power model. Coordinates are an approximate road-intersection geocode near North Brown Road, not a parcel-confirmed point.

properties.notes: Proposed in Cerro Gordo County adjacent to Alliant's Emery Generating Station, expected operational in 2031 pending regulatory approval. properties.name: ScaleMatrix San Diego
properties.notes: ScaleMatrix's own site discloses '5MW aggregate availability; 20MW+ utility upgrade capacity' - the widely-repeated flat '20MW' figure on aggregator sites is the future upgrade ceiling, not installed/operational capacity; cross-validated by an independent SDG&E-sourced interconnection record showing <10MW. A May 2026 expansion added 46,000 sq ft to the ~50,000 sq ft Kearny Mesa campus (~96,000 sq ft total) - this 'doubling' is square footage, not MW capacity. aiClassification set to 'likely': ScaleMatrix markets GPU-as-a-Service explicitly for HPC/deep learning/AI workloads, and this San Diego site is confirmed as the location of a ScaleMatrix/HPE 'Hybrid HPC Center of Excellence.' Address confirmed via a Washington-state LLC filing and parcel records; this is the company's headquarters campus, operating since approximately 2011-2012 in the Kearny Mesa neighborhood of the City of San Diego.

properties.name: Scott Data Center
properties.notes: Tier III colocation facility on the Scott Technology Campus in Omaha (Douglas County), adjacent to the University of Nebraska at Omaha's Peter Kiewit Institute. Unusual ownership for the dataset: Scott Data describes itself as a NONPROFIT data center founded by Walter Scott Jr. Certified/aligned to Tier III design, Energy Star, AICPA SOC and NIST; supports 60+ kW cabinets and deployments from kilowatts to multi-megawatt — the high-density-cabinet capability is the only AI-relevant signal published. capacityMw and square footage are deliberately OMITTED: the widely repeated '110,000 sq ft' and '20 MW central plant' figures come from colocation directories that were NOT fetched this session, and the operator's own page publishes neither. ADDRESS DISCREPANCY left visible: the operator's own site gives 6825 Pine Street while third-party directories list 6805 Pine Street — the operator's figure is used and the conflict noted rather than silently reconciled. Coordinates are an approximation of the Peter Kiewit Institute / Scott Technology Campus area, not a parcel geocode. confidence is 'reported' — single source.

properties.name: Servpac MTP Building 2
properties.notes: Located in Mililani Technology Park, Central O'ahu, 10 miles inland and 850 feet above sea level, outside major flood, tsunami, and hurricane zones. Building 2 will approximately 10x the existing 1MW IT capacity of MTP Building 1 (Hawaii's only Uptime Institute Tier IV certified facility). Designed to withstand Category 5 hurricane-force winds. Primary use is enterprise colocation; no AI-specific tenant announced. DCD (February 2026) reports project is in design phase; 'broke ground' claim in original record is unsupported by the cited source. Hawaii's structural barriers (highest US electricity costs, limited grid capacity) make large-scale hyperscale AI builds unlikely; Servpac MTP2 is the only Hawaii project of note found.

properties.name: T5@Silicon Valley
properties.notes: Operator corrected to T5 Data Centers, not Serverfarm: Serverfarm's own current locations page does not list a Newark/Silicon Valley property, and Serverfarm has acquired only one T5 property to date (El Segundo/LAX1, already tracked separately as serverfarm-lax1-el-segundo-ca) - not a company-wide rebrand. T5 Data Centers remains an active, independent company. The existing 128,000 SF/17MW building (built 2002 per county assessor record) was sold by Apple to T5 in an Aug 2020 ($30M) deed transfer, announced by T5 Oct 6 2020 alongside a disclosed plan to add 32.1MW/180,000 SF (49.1MW total target); no source confirms whether that expansion has completed. The $30M figure is a real-estate acquisition price for the existing building only, not development capex, so it is not recorded as investmentUsd. Apple as tenant is corroborated by secondary sources (an aggregator listing and a contractor's own portfolio page naming Apple independently) but not by a primary T5/Apple source, which refers only to 'a Fortune 100 enterprise' - flagged reported, not primary-confirmed. No AI/HPC/GPU-specific marketing found, so aiClassification is omitted. T5 markets this campus as 'Silicon Valley,' but Newark is geographically East Bay/Alameda County, not South Bay/Santa Clara County. Coordinates are a best-effort approximate estimate for the disclosed street address, not an independently geocoded parcel point - recommend a follow-up pass with a mapping source to confirm precisely.

properties.name: Tenaska Southeast Nebraska Power Plant (proposed)
properties.notes: The dedicated-generation half of the proposed Google/Tenaska southeast-Nebraska campus already tracked as google-nebraska-ai-campus-proposed, split into its own record per the dataset's same-site power+compute convention (cf. alterra-marshall-technology-energy-center-gas-mi). Tenaska (Omaha-based) would build and operate a privately owned combined-cycle natural gas plant sized at 1,000-3,000 MW — at the top of that range larger than Gerald Gentleman Station, Nebraska's largest existing plant. A Tenaska representative told Otoe County landowner Rick Wheatley the company was assembling roughly 2,000 acres near a gas pipeline for a plant that could serve an AI center; landAcres records that stated assembly TARGET, not a purchased parcel. capacityMw.planned uses the LOW end (1,000 MW) of the reported range. Carbon capture is planned with Tallgrass Energy named as a possible CO2 transporter — Tallgrass has publicly denied any current partnership, so that link is recorded as reported-and-denied, not as fact. The project depends on passage of Nebraska LB1261, which would let privately owned plants interconnect to public power district grids and sell excess power back. No site has been fixed: Tenaska holds options across Gage (1,509 ac), Otoe (1,454 ac), Cass (1,123 ac) and Lancaster (~680 ac) counties. Coordinates mirror the approximate Otoe/Gage search-area centroid already used on the paired compute record — NOT a siting-confirmed point.

properties.notes: Site north of Milan-Oakville Road, east of Hitchingham Road, Augusta Township, Washtenaw County MI (between Ann Arbor and Monroe). No end user announced; planners cited Google and Microsoft as typical users of this facility type. Form8tion is Thor's digital infrastructure arm (founded March 2023). Capacity not disclosed; at least five large buildings planned. Voter referendum outcome will determine project viability. Coordinates are approximate Augusta Township centroid. SOURCE CONFLICT RESOLVED 2026-08-08: the earlier "rejected by voters" claim in an article predating the election was a pre-election piece describing the UPCOMING vote — the dates now reconcile because the referendum has since been held. Augusta Township voters overturned the 522-acre rezoning on 2026-08-04 (about 90% to overturn), so the parcels revert to agricultural residential. Recorded as "cancelled" because the project's enabling rezoning is gone; note that Thor Equities has NOT publicly withdrawn, and the results were unofficial as of 2026-08-05 — revisit if the developer re-applies or the count is certified differently.

properties.name: Buckeye Tech Corridor
properties.notes: Master-planned data center park on a ~2,069-acre former residential (Cipriani) parcel Tract acquired for ~$136M, south of I-10 in Buckeye; planned for up to ~20M sq ft across as many as 40 data centers at full build-out over ~15 years (~$20B). Coordinates are an approximate town-level geocode (Buckeye, south of I-10), not a parcel-confirmed point. The City of Buckeye executed a development agreement with AZLCO Buckeye, LLC (Ordinance No. 08-24, adopted unanimously 2024-08-06). It reimburses the developer for six enumerated regional infrastructure components it builds and dedicates to the city — two public-safety sites, temporary and permanent public-safety facilities, $15M toward the Johnson Road interchange, and oversized regional water infrastructure — funded by 20% of the tax revenue the project itself generates, beginning only after the city has received $60M cumulatively and terminating 20 years from the effective date. It is capped at "the lesser of" the developer's verified costs or $50,000,000, so it cannot exceed what the developer actually spent; it is cost recovery for public infrastructure rather than an incentive, abatement or credit, and is therefore not recorded as a subsidy. Nothing has been paid to date. Buckeye's economic-development director has projected "more than 360 jobs at full build out" — an end-state across as many as 40 separate future data centers, none yet leased, permitted or built, and so not recorded as a permanent-jobs figure for this site. A search of 226 Buckeye Council and P&Z agendas (Feb 2024 – Aug 2026) found no GPLET and no Foreign Trade Zone instrument.

properties.notes: Denver-based land developer Tract's speculative hyperscale campus at the former Fountain Valley Golf Club (2830 220th St W) plus adjacent Farmington school-district land, Dakota County. Facility scope: up to 12 buildings, 2.5M+ sq ft, plus 2 admin buildings. Coordinates are an approximate estimate for 220th St W south of downtown Farmington — not geocoded this session, verify before publish. Operating entities: MNLCO Farmington LLC / MNLCO Farmington Two LLC.

properties.notes: Vermaland LLC is a Phoenix-area land developer and land-banking company (CEO Kuldip 'Ken' Verma, founded 2006, controls ~25,000 acres of metro Phoenix land). DCD explicitly noted 'it is unclear whether Vermaland would operate its own data center facilities' — Vermaland plans to sell or rent parcels/buildings to tenants. No end tenants or hyperscaler operators have been named as of July 2026. Original plan: 59 data centers, up to 3 GW capacity ceiling, up to $33B investment ceiling, 3,300-acre site south of Eloy along the Greene Canal. A separate adjacent 1,700-acre parcel already holds Industrial-2 zoning for data centers, gas plants, battery storage, and solar. After strong public opposition (all ~60 public comments opposed), operator announced May 2026 scale-back to 11 data centers and 1 GW ceiling. Board of Supervisors hearing scheduled August 26, 2026; no permits issued as of record date. Site lies adjacent to a Qualified Opportunity Zone (investor tax benefit; not a direct subsidy to Vermaland — no subsidy award confirmed, omitted). Coordinates are approximate (parcel south of Eloy city center along Greene Canal; no precise APN published). $33B investment and all GW figures are announced ceilings, not firm commitments.
